title: Some cellular automata make even average properties hard to predict

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Some cellular automata make even average properties hard to predict

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Some simple cellular automata, such as rule 110, are more complex than random-looking ones like rule 30: they mix regular regions with interacting localized structures, so that even average properties of their behavior become very difficult to predict.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: there are cellular automata whose behavior is in effect still more complex—and in which even such averages become very difficult to predict.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 2, “The Crucial Experiment”; section “How Do Simple Programs Behave?” (from p. 23), p. 31. Scope: elementary cellular automata with localized structures, especially rule 110

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch02-06: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Exact trajectories and extensive computational comparisons are feasible. The comparative complexity language and absence of general prediction lower bounds leave the broad statement only partly resolved.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Specify average observables and prediction horizons for rule 110 and rule 30, then benchmark prediction algorithms against direct simulation and uncertainty baselines. Higher irreducible cost or forecast error for rule 110 would support the comparative claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
More complex and very difficult depend on the observable and algorithm.

Failure to find a predictor is not a lower-bound proof.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.55
analysis feasibility: 0.7
data adequacy: 0.75
data existence: 1.0
discriminating power: 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Both rules are elementary and fully specified, so ensembles of their averages can be generated and scored with ordinary statistics in days. A pre-registered gap in prediction error separates the claim from the rival that rule 110 is merely random-looking in the same way as rule 30. The word 'very difficult' still needs a numeric threshold, which is why discriminating power is only moderate.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare rule 110 with rule 30 on the predictability of averages, such as density and block frequencies, using predictors that are cheaper than simulation. The claim is confirmed if those averages for rule 110 stay substantially harder to forecast while the pattern also shows persistent localized structures, and refuted if the averages are as predictable as rule 30's.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Some spatial averages of rule 110 converge even when individual structures remain hard to track.

Difficulty of prediction depends on the predictor class and the horizon.
